Experimental / Communities

Bring the card to your community

What a community needs to run Fedimint Card, two ways to start, and the steps of a first pilot. Fedimint Card is an experimental prototype, tested with small amounts on one federation.

  • Federation
  • Till
  • POS app
  • Cards
  • Setup app

What you need

  • A federation. Your community’s Fedimint federation with a Bitcoin mint v1 or v2 module. Its guardians check each payment and mark the notes spent. Your guardians run it.
  • A till. A Card 4.0 merchant till with a wallet in your federation. It builds each payment and sends it to the federation, and its wallet receives what merchants are paid. It sits on the merchants' side, and your community decides who runs it.
  • The POS app. Use the signed Card 4.0 Android POS app for a new install. The store channels are Google Play, TestFlight. The app reads the card by NFC, takes the PIN and passes the card's answers to the till. Each merchant installs it.
  • Cards. Compatible contactless cards with the Card 4.x applet, such as the J3R180 or J3R452. Each holder gets one card and its PIN.
  • The Setup app. Fedimint Card Setup, on the phone of the person who issues cards (Google Play, TestFlight). It sets up a blank card in one tap, and it approves your tills.

Check with your issuer that your cards and registry support Card 4.0 and your federation’s mint. The till uses registry.fedimintcard.org by default. The registry records the notes associated with each card (see Privacy). The Setup app signs in to an operator account on the registry, and only the people who run the registry can make one.

Two ways to start

01 / Ready-made

Cards set up for your federation

Cards are set up for your federation and shipped to you. They are offered at cost to pilot communities.

Write to hi@fedimintcard.org

02 / Do it yourself

Blank cards and the open guides

Buy blank J3R180 cards and set them up with the Setup app. The guides and the code are public, starting from the developers page.

Where to get blank cards

A pilot, step by step

  1. Decide who runs the till

    Choose the person who will run the till. Its wallet receives what merchants are paid. To connect the till to the registry, the till shows a QR code and a short code, and the card issuer approves it in the Setup app under Settings, then Tills, then Add a till.

  2. Put the POS app on the first merchants' phones

    Install Fedimint Card POS on each merchant's phone and pair it with the till. The till shows a pairing QR code, and the merchant scans it with Pair with till in the POS settings. The phone needs a connection to pair and sync.

  3. Get cards

    Use ready-made cards, or set up blank cards with the Setup app, one tap per card, in batches. Each card makes its own keys on its chip and gets a PIN of 4 to 8 digits.

  4. Hand out cards with their PINs

    Give each holder their card and its PIN. Ask holders to keep their PIN private and carry only small amounts.

  5. Top up

    On the POS, read the card and tap Top up card. Enter an amount in sats and tap Review top-up. The holder checks the card credit, fixed top-up fee and total, then chooses Show payment QR. After paying that invoice, tap the card to load the quoted credit.

  6. Take the first payment

    Tap Charge card and type the price. The holder types the PIN on the merchant's phone and taps the card. The card signs the payment and the federation settles it.

  7. Check after the first day

    Look at the till's list of sales and its status, which shows the federation, the wallet balance, the card link and the registry. A disconnected POS phone keeps eligible offline payments until it can sync. Reconnect each phone and confirm that its payments settle. Follow the till backup guide for its wallet and payment records.

What it costs to run

  • Cards. One blank J3R180 card for each holder. Where to get cards lists prices as they were on 23 October 2026.
  • A machine for the till. A server that runs the till and its wallet. Install the StartOS package or Docker image.
  • Phones. An NFC phone for each merchant, and one for the person who sets up cards.
  • The federation's fees. The POS quotes a fixed customer fee that covers receiving the Lightning payment and loading the card. Any fee left after costs stays with the merchant. The sending wallet may quote its own routing fee.

What to tell holders and merchants

Fedimint Card is an experimental prototype, and its applet and till code have had no outside security review. Keep only small amounts on a card, amounts you can afford to lose.

For holders

  • The federation holds the bitcoin.
  • A lost or wiped card loses its eCash.
  • Keep the card’s PIN private.
  • Pay only at tills you trust.
  • The registry can see balances.
  • The Fedi app cannot load cards.

For merchants

  • Some amounts cannot be paid.
  • Top-ups round to card amounts.
  • Offline payments settle later.
  • The apps are public betas.

Risks to know explains each one.
